# Quick manual verification of m1 behavior
import arrow
from dateutil import tz as dateutil_tz

# Test 1: Normal shift should work the same
arw = arrow.get(2023, 1, 1)
result1 = arw.shift(days=1)
result2 = arw.shift(days=1, check_imaginary=True)
result3 = arw.shift(days=1, check_imaginary=False)
print(f"Normal shift: {result1} == {result2} == {result3}: {result1 == result2 == result3}")

# Test 2: DST spring-forward (US/Pacific, March 12, 2023 at 2AM -> 3AM)
# Before DST: 2023-03-11 01:30 PST
# After shifting 1 hour forward, we'd land in the "imaginary" gap (2:00-3:00 AM doesn't exist)
arw_pacific = arrow.Arrow(2023, 3, 11, 1, 30, tzinfo=dateutil_tz.gettz('US/Pacific'))
print(f"Before DST: {arw_pacific}")

# Shift 1 hour - this lands in imaginary time (2:00 AM doesn't exist in Pacific on March 12, 2023)
result_default = arw_pacific.shift(hours=1)
result_false = arw_pacific.shift(hours=1, check_imaginary=False)
result_true = arw_pacific.shift(hours=1, check_imaginary=True)

print(f"Default (check_imaginary=True): {result_default}")
print(f"check_imaginary=False: {result_false}")
print(f"check_imaginary=True explicit: {result_true}")
print(f"Default == True: {result_default == result_true}")
print(f"False != Default: {result_false != result_default}")
